$comment: Demo scenarios generated by generate.sh. args are passed to qloggen (see main.go or qloggen -h). dir is relative to public/examples/. demo: the file the app's manifest points to ('qlog' = the merged client+server .qlog, 'server' = the server .sqlog). fixture: also copy the files to tests/fixtures/latest/.

scenarios.title: new_cid: connection ID updates
scenarios.description: A single 20 KB HTTP/3 GET over a 30 ms RTT path without loss. Right after the handshake, both endpoints issue NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames, switch to a connection ID of the peer and retire the previous one (RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID); quic:connection_id_updated events mark every change. Client and server trace of the same connection.

scenarios.title: 10 parallel streams: 10 x 50 KB with 5% loss
scenarios.description: Ten parallel HTTP/3 GETs of 50 KB each on one connection, over a 40 ms RTT path with 5% random packet loss in both directions (the equivalent of qvis' parallel_10_50KB demo). Shows stream multiplexing, retransmissions and loss recovery. Client and server trace of the same connection.

scenarios.title: Double vantage point, 100 ms RTT
scenarios.description: The client and the server trace of one connection in a single file: a 1 MB HTTP/3 download over a 100 ms RTT, 20 Mbit/s path with 1% random loss in both directions. Both traces use the system clock with a real epoch, so they can be aligned in time; packets lost on the path appear in only one of the traces.

scenarios.title: Congestion control: 6 x 300 KB through a 4 Mbit/s bottleneck with 2% loss
scenarios.description: Six parallel 300 KB HTTP/3 responses through a 4 Mbit/s bottleneck (50 ms RTT, drop-tail buffer of one bandwidth-delay product) with 2% random loss in both directions. Slow start overshoots the bottleneck buffer, the queue raises the RTT, and the congestion window then alternates between recovery and congestion avoidance. Client and server trace of the same connection.

scenarios.title: Baseline: one 1 MB download without loss
scenarios.description: A single 1 MB HTTP/3 GET over a 40 ms RTT path without loss or bandwidth limit: handshake, connection ID updates, slow start and a clean connection close. Client and server trace of the same connection.

scenarios.title: Massive trace: 50 MB download
scenarios.description: A 50 MB HTTP/3 download over a 20 ms RTT path with a 100 Mbit/s bottleneck and no random loss (packets are only lost when the bottleneck buffer overflows), for performance testing. This is the server trace; the client trace of the same connection is next to it.
